name: North Rhine-Westphalia
summary: Green, white and red horizontal bands with the state arms: a white wavy line on green for the Rhine, the white Westphalian horse on red, and the red rose of Lippe.
origin: North Rhine-Westphalia was created by the British in 1946 from the northern Rhine Province and Westphalia, and Lippe joined in 1947. The colours combine the green and white of the Rhineland and the red and white of Westphalia; the arms were adopted in 1953.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Shared by the Rhineland and Westphalia.

symbols.name: Rhine
symbols.description: A white wavy diagonal line on green.

facts: It is Germany's most populous state.
Its capital is Düsseldorf, though Cologne is the largest city.
The plain tricolour is the civil flag.
clues: Green, white and red bands with arms showing a river, a horse and a rose.
Its colours combine the Rhineland and Westphalia.
